name: Poulet DG
summary: Cameroonian chicken stewed with fried ripe plantain, carrots, peppers and green beans in a savoury tomato sauce.
story: Poulet DG, meaning the Director General's chicken, is a festive Cameroonian dish associated with special occasions, restaurants and gatherings, partly because chicken and plantain were once considered luxuries. The name is commonly explained as a dish fit for a company director. It is served with extra plantain or rice.

items.name: Very ripe plantains
items.note: peeled, cut in thick diagonal slices

steps.title: Boil the chicken
steps.text: Put the chicken, quartered onion, garlic, ginger, thyme, bay, bouillon and salt in a pot with water just to cover. Simmer 25 minutes until cooked through, then lift out and keep the stock.

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.text: Heat 4 tablespoons of oil in a wide pan and fry the chicken for 8 minutes, turning, until the skin is golden. Remove and set aside.

steps.title: Fry the plantain
steps.text: Heat the plantain oil to medium-high and fry the slices in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side. They are ready when deep golden and caramelised at the edges. Drain on paper.

steps.title: Sauté vegetables
steps.text: In the chicken pan, cook the sliced onion 4 minutes, then add the carrots, celery and green beans and cook 5 minutes. They should stay slightly crisp.

steps.title: Add the sauce
steps.text: Stir in the tomato paste, then the blended tomatoes and scotch bonnet, and cook 10 to 12 minutes until the sauce thickens and the oil separates.

steps.title: Simmer together
steps.text: Return the chicken to the pan with the pepper and 150 ml of the reserved stock. Cover and simmer 8 to 10 minutes until the vegetables are just tender and the sauce coats the chicken.

steps.title: Add plantain
steps.text: Fold in half the fried plantain gently so it keeps its shape and cook 2 minutes. Remove the scotch bonnet and taste for salt.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile into a serving dish with the remaining plantain on top. Serve warm, with rice if you like.

tips: Use plantains that are almost fully black-yellow and soft, as they caramelise and sweeten the sauce.
Add the green beans and pepper late so they keep colour and bite.
Leave the scotch bonnet whole for flavour with only mild heat; burst it for more.
Keep the chicken stock; it makes a good base for rice.

swaps.swap: Firm bananas are too soft; use semi-ripe plantains or fry thick slices of sweet potato.
Habanero, or a whole red chilli for gentler heat.
One 400 g tin of chopped tomatoes.
